svg.title: Chart C · Non-kinetic operations
svg.desc: Bars: sustained campaigns. Points: discrete events. Arrowhead: ongoing. Solid: official or multi-government attribution. Outline: researcher / open-source attribution. Dashed outline: alleged. Attribution is recorded as the source states it.
svg.text: Data as of SWF 9th ed. (Apr. 2026) · Source: SWF 2026 and ledger

svg.desc: Swimlane chart of non-kinetic counterspace operations by category. Bars are sustained campaigns; points are discrete events; arrowheads mark ongoing campaigns. Solid fill means official or multi-government attribution, outline means researcher or open-source attribution, dashed outline means alleged. A data table follows the chart.

text.tspan: SWF 2026: only non-destructive capabilities are actively
used against satellites in current military operations.
The rules that govern them are soft law (expert manuals)
or carry military exemptions (ITU Constitution Art. 48).

g.aria-label: Iran (jamming from Cuba; later Bulgaria, Libya): Telstar 12 Persian-language broadcasts. 2003 to 2006. Attribution: Alleged (unconfirmed).
Iran: Eutelsat satellites carrying BBC Persian and Voice of America. 2009 to 2012. Attribution: Multiple governments / intergovernmental body.

text.tspan: Iran: Eutelsat satellites carrying BBC Persian and Voice of America

g.aria-label: Russia: Starlink user terminals in Ukraine. 2022 to ongoing. Attribution: Alleged (unconfirmed).

text.tspan: Russia: Starlink user terminals in Ukraine

g.aria-label: Russia (origin locations cited by ITU RRB): Swedish and French broadcasting satellites. 2024 to ongoing. Attribution: Multiple governments / intergovernmental body.

text.tspan: Russia: Swedish and French broadcasting satellites

g.aria-label: Iraq: GPS receivers of coalition munitions and aircraft. 2003 to 2003. Attribution: Official (single government).

text.tspan: Iraq: GPS receivers of coalition munitions and aircraft

g.aria-label: North Korea: GPS receivers of aircraft, ships and vehicles in South Korea. 2010 to ongoing. Attribution: Official (single government).

text.tspan: North Korea: GPS receivers of aircraft, ships and vehicles in South Korea

g.aria-label: Russia: GNSS receivers in Ukraine, Crimea and the Black Sea. 2014 to ongoing. Attribution: Researcher / open-source analysis.

text.tspan: Russia: GNSS receivers in Ukraine, Crimea and the Black Sea

g.aria-label: Russia: GNSS receivers in and around Syria and the eastern Mediterranean. 2016 to ongoing. Attribution: Researcher / open-source analysis.

text.tspan: Russia: GNSS receivers in and around Syria and the eastern Mediterranean

g.aria-label: Russia: GPS receivers in northern Norway and Finland during NATO Trident Juncture. 2018 to 2018. Attribution: Official (single government).

text.tspan: Russia: GPS receivers in northern Norway and Finland during NATO Trident Juncture

g.aria-label: Israel (IDF): GNSS receivers of aircraft over Israel and neighboring states. 2023 to ongoing. Attribution: Official (single government).

text.tspan: Israel: GNSS receivers of aircraft over Israel and neighboring states

g.aria-label: Russia: GNSS receivers of civil aircraft and ships over the Baltic region. 2023 to ongoing. Attribution: Multiple governments / intergovernmental body. Opens 3D scene.

text.tspan: Russia: GNSS receivers of civil aircraft and ships over the Baltic region

g.aria-label: United States: MSTI-3 (retired USAF experimental satellite). Oct 17, 1997. Attribution: Official (single government). Opens 3D scene.
China: US optical imaging satellites. Jan 1, 2006. Attribution: Alleged (unconfirmed).
Russia: Satellites overflying Russian mobile ICBM units (stated purpose). Mar 1, 2018. Attribution: Official (single government). Opens 3D scene.

text.tspan: Russia: Satellites overflying Russian mobile ICBM units

g.aria-label: Russia: Viasat KA-SAT user terminals (modems) and management network. Feb 24, 2022. Attribution: Multiple governments / intergovernmental body. Opens 3D scene.

svg.text: Bars: sustained campaigns. Points: discrete events. Arrowhead: ongoing. Solid: official or multi-government attribution. Outline: researcher / open-source attribution. Dashed outline: alleged. Attribution is recorded

Source: Secure World Foundation, Global Counterspace Capabilities: An Open Source Assessment (9th ed., Apr. 2026) and the primary sources cited in the ledger. Data as of SWF 9th ed. (Apr. 2026). Companion to
Space Security Law: Governance Beyond the Atmosphere.
